question: A seller makes a loss of 5% by selling a shirt for ₹1,000. He would have made x% profit by selling for ₹1,400. Find the value of x.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss 5% ⇒ SP = 95% of CP

1000 = 0.95 × CP ⇒ CP = 1000 ÷ 0.95 = 1052.63

Profit at 1400 = 1400 − 1052.63 = 347.37

Profit % = (347.37 / 1052.63) × 100 ≈ 33%

**∴ Answer = 33%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss = 5%, SP₁ = 1000

New SP₂ = 1400

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 − loss%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP₁ = CP × 0.95

⇒ 1000 = 0.95 × CP

⇒ CP = 1000 ÷ 0.95 = 1052.63

⇒ Profit = 1400 − 1052.63 = 347.37

⇒ Profit% = (347.37 ÷ 1052.63) × 100 ≈ 33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

SP = CP × (1 − loss%)

Profit Formula

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Reverse Method

Find CP first, then new profit

Key Insight

Same CP used for both selling prices
